fullPassage: The kitchen tap makes strange sounds. It coughs. It spits once, and then goes silent. “Mom,” I shout out into the living room, “water is not coming out.” “Alyssa, shush!” Mom says. She is watching the TV, where a news anchor is talking about the “flow crisis.” This is what the media has been calling the drought ever since people got tired of hearing the word “drought.” Now the crisis is entering a new stage. We have no running water out of the tap. “To the mall!” says Uncle Basil. My little brother Garrett and I jump in our uncle’s truck. As we pull into the parking lot, we can see the crowd. “You two go in. I’ll meet you inside,” Uncle Basil says. Inside it’s like Black Friday at its worst — but today it’s not televisions and video games people are after. What I see in the carts in the checkout line are mostly water bottles. The essentials of life. There is a look of impatience on the faces of the people in line. There is even hostility, hidden by a thin layer of politeness. Even that politeness is stretched thin. As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize I am too late. The shelves are already empty. I manage my way to the side aisle, trying my luck. Sometimes people place unwanted items in the wrong shelves. Lucky! I find a single case of water that someone abandoned there maybe yesterday, when it wasn’t such a precious commodity. I reach for it, only to find it pulled away at the last second by a woman. She stacks it on top of her cart like a crown on top of her canned goods. “I’m sorry, but we were here first,” she says. And then her daughter steps forward — a girl I recognize from soccer — Hali Hartling. As her mother pulls their cart away, Hali leans closer to me. “I’m sorry about that, Alyssa.” “Didn’t I share my water with you at the practice last week?” I point out to her. “Maybe you could return the favor and share a few bottles with me.” She looks back to her mother, who’s already moving down the aisle, then turns back to me shaking her head. And then she gets a little bit red in the face, and turns to leave before it becomes a deep flush. I look for Garrett, whom I find in the frozen aisle. Then I see something. Just past the frozen vegetables and ice cream, there is a case packed with ice. I open the door and reach for a bag. “What are you doing? We need water, not ice,” he reminds me. “Ice is water. Just help me,” I tell him. Garrett and I put one bag of ice after another into our cart, until it is piled as high as it can get. By now other people have taken notice and begin to empty the ice case. The cart is ridiculously heavy now, and almost impossible to push. Then, a man in a business suit comes up behind us. He smiles. “Looks like you could use some help.” He doesn’t wait for us to answer before grabbing the cart’s handle. “Thank you for helping us,” I tell him. “Not a problem. We all need to help one another.” He smiles again, and I return the smile. It is good to know that difficult times can bring out the best in people. I decide that one favor deserves another. “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourself,” I suggest. His smile does not fade. “I have a better idea,” he says. “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourselves, and I’ll keep the rest.” Alyssa.” For a moment I think he is joking, but then realize he is serious. “Excuse me?” He is still smiling, but his eyes scare me. As long as his hands are firmly locked on the handle of our cart, there is nothing to prove that it’s ours and not his. “Is there a problem here?” It is Uncle Basil. He has arrived just in time. “Not at all.” The man looks at the ice with a bitter face, then leaves. *The above is a shortened version of the opening of the novel Dry (2018). It tells the story of a girl who has to make tough choices for her family during a disastrous California drought. Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal. Provided that the factors contributing to water shortages worldwide are not addressed, including climate change, population growth, and using too much water for agriculture, it is possible that this story can become a reality. Further Reading Hunger Stones In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought in 500 years in Europe, a stone known as a “hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along the Elbe River. The stone had a sentence written on it that read: “If you see me, then cry.” The hunger stones, found in rivers across central Europe, typically remain underwater. However, when droughts occur and water levels retreat, these stones become visible. The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts. Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor. The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be prepared. Considering the continuation of climate change, experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could persist for decades. The United Nations has predicted that by 2050, 75 percent of the global population could suffer from the effects of drought unless significant action is taken to address climate change.

I’ll meet you inside,” Uncle Basil says.  Inside it’s like Black Friday at ③<u>its</u> worst — but today it’s not televisions and video games people are ④<u>after</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① jumps → jump: 주어가 'Garrett and I(개럿과 나)'로 두 명(복수)이라 동사에 -s를 붙이지 않고 원형 jump를 써요
det.analysis:
① jumps → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'My little brother Garrett and I jump in our uncle's truck'는 '내 남동생 개럿과 나는 삼촌의 트럭에 올라탄다'예요. 주어가 'Garrett and I'로 두 사람(복수)이에요. 복수 주어에는 동사에 -s를 붙이지 않아요. 그래서 jumps가 아니라 jump가 맞아요. ❌ jumps는 틀림 ←정답

② pull: 'As we pull into the parking lot'은 '우리가 주차장으로 들어설 때'예요. 주어 we(우리)가 복수라 원형 pull이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ its: 'like Black Friday at its worst'는 '최악의 블랙 프라이데이처럼'이에요. its는 '그것의'라는 소유격(=of it)이에요. it's(it is의 줄임말)와 헷갈리기 쉽지만, 여기서는 '그것의 최악'이라는 소유의 뜻이라 its가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ after: 'it's not televisions and video games people are after'는 '사람들이 원하는 것은 텔레비전이나 비디오 게임이 아니다'예요. be after는 '~을 원하다/좇다'라는 뜻의 표현이라 여기서 after가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 주어가 'A and B(두 명)'면 복수 → 동사에 -s 안 붙임(jump)

questions.passage: ” She ①<u>looks</u> back to her mother, who’s already ②<u>moving</u> down the aisle, then turns back to me ③<u>shaken</u> her head.  And then she gets a little bit red in the face, and turns to leave before it becomes a deep flush.  I look for Garrett, whom I find in the frozen aisle.  Then I see something.  Just past the frozen vegetables and ice cream, there is a case ④<u>packed</u> with ice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ shaken → shaking: '그녀가 고개를 젓는' 것은 그녀가 스스로 하는 능동적 동작이라 현재분사(-ing) shaking
det.analysis:
① looks: 'She looks back to her mother'는 '그녀는 어머니를 돌아본다'예요. 주어 She(그녀, 3인칭 단수)라서 동사에 -s를 붙인 looks가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② moving: 'her mother, who's already moving down the aisle'는 '통로를 따라 이미 걸어가고 있는 그녀의 어머니'예요. who's는 who is의 줄임말이고, '~하고 있는 중'이라는 진행의 뜻이라 -ing인 moving이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ shaken → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'then turns back to me shaking her head'는 '그러고는 고개를 저으며 나에게 돌아선다'예요. 고개를 젓는 동작은 그녀가 스스로 하는 능동적인 행동이에요. 이렇게 '~하면서'라는 뜻으로 동작을 함께 나타낼 때는 현재분사(-ing) shaking을 써요. 과거분사 shaken은 '흔들린(당한)'이라는 수동의 뜻이라 여기엔 안 맞아요. 그래서 shaking으로 고쳐야 해요. ❌ shaken은 틀림 ←정답

④ packed: 'there is a case packed with ice'는 '얼음으로 가득 채워진 상자가 하나 있다'예요. 상자는 얼음으로 '채워지는' 쪽(수동)이라 과거분사 packed가 앞의 case를 꾸며 주어 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: '~하면서'(스스로 하는 동작)는 현재분사 -ing → shaking(고개를 저으며)

questions.passage: ” The man looks at the ice with a bitter face, then leaves.  *The above is a ①<u>shortened</u> version of the opening of the novel Dry (2018).  It tells the story of a girl who has to make tough choices for her family during a disastrous California drought.  Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal.  Provided that the factors ②<u>contributed</u> to water shortages worldwide are not ③<u>addressed</u>, including climate change, population growth, and ④<u>using</u> too much water for agriculture, it is possible that this story can become a reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② contributed → contributing: '요인들'이 물 부족을 '유발하는' 능동의 뜻이라 현재분사(-ing) contributing을 써서 the factors를 꾸며 줘요
det.analysis:
① shortened: 'The above is a shortened version of the opening of the novel Dry'는 '위 글은 소설 Dry 도입부의 축약된 판본이다'예요. 판본은 '줄여진(축약된)' 쪽(수동)이라 과거분사 shortened가 version을 꾸며 주어 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② contributed → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 원문은 'the factors contributing to water shortages worldwide(전 세계 물 부족의 원인이 되는 요인들)'예요. 밑줄 친 말은 앞의 명사 'the factors(요인들)'를 꾸며 줘요. 요인들은 물 부족을 '일으키는(유발하는)' 쪽이라 능동의 뜻이에요. 명사를 꾸미면서 '~하는'이라는 능동을 나타낼 때는 현재분사(-ing) contributing을 써요. 과거분사 contributed는 '기여된(당한)'이라는 수동의 뜻이라 여기엔 안 맞아요. 그래서 contributing으로 고쳐야 해요. ❌ contributed는 틀림 ←정답

③ addressed: 'the factors ... are not addressed'는 '그 요인들이 해결되지 않으면'이에요. 요인들은 사람에 의해 '해결되는' 쪽(수동)이라 be동사(are) 뒤에 과거분사 addressed를 써서 수동태를 만들어요. ✅ 올바름

④ using: 'including climate change, population growth, and using too much water'는 '기후 변화, 인구 증가, 그리고 물을 너무 많이 쓰는 것을 포함하여'예요. 앞의 명사들과 나란히 이어지는 자리라 동명사(-ing) using이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 명사를 꾸미며 '~하는'(능동)이면 현재분사 -ing → the factors contributing(원인이 되는 요인들)

questions.passage: There is a look of ①<u>impatience</u> on the faces of the people in line.  There is even ②<u>hostility</u>, hidden by a thin layer of politeness.  Even that politeness is stretched thin.  As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize I am too ③<u>late</u>.  The shelves are already ④<u>full</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ full → empty: 물을 사러 왔지만 '너무 늦었다(too late)'고 했으니 선반은 이미 '텅 빈(empty)' 상태여야 해요
det.analysis:
① impatience: 'There is a look of impatience on the faces of the people in line'은 '줄 선 사람들의 얼굴에는 초조함이 어려 있다'예요. 물이 부족해 다급한 상황이라 '초조함(impatience)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② hostility: 'There is even hostility, hidden by a thin layer of politeness'는 '얇은 예의로 가려진 적대감마저 있다'예요. 서로 물을 차지하려는 긴장된 분위기라 '적대감(hostility)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ late: 'As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize I am too late'는 '생수를 사러 가게 뒤편으로 가면서, 내가 너무 늦었다는 걸 깨닫는다'예요. 뒤에 선반이 비었다는 내용이 이어지니 '늦었다(late)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ full → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'The shelves are already empty'로 '선반은 이미 텅 비어 있다'예요. 앞에서 '너무 늦었다'고 했으니 물이 다 팔려 선반이 '비어 있어야(empty)' 앞뒤가 맞아요. full(가득 찬)은 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: '너무 늦었다' → 물이 다 팔려 선반이 텅 빔(empty), 가득 참(full)은 반대

questions.passage: ” The hunger stones, found in rivers across central Europe, typically remain underwater.  However, when droughts occur and water levels ①<u>retreat</u>, these stones become ②<u>visible</u>.  The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts.  Droughts cause ③<u>increased</u> harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor.  The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be ④<u>prepared</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ increased → reduced: 가뭄은 수확을 '줄이는' 것이라 reduced(줄어든). 뒤에 이어지는 '식량 부족·굶주림'과도 이어져야 해요
det.analysis:
① retreat: 'when droughts occur and water levels retreat'는 '가뭄이 들고 수위가 물러날(낮아질) 때'예요. 가뭄이면 물이 줄어드니 '물러나다(retreat)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

② visible: 'these stones become visible'은 '이 돌들이 눈에 보이게 된다'예요. 물이 낮아지면 물속에 잠겨 있던 돌이 드러나니 '보이는(visible)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ increased → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger'로 '가뭄은 수확 감소, 식량 부족, 굶주림을 일으킨다'예요. 가뭄이 들면 농사가 안 되어 수확이 '줄어들어야(reduced)' 뒤의 '식량 부족'과 '굶주림'으로 자연스럽게 이어져요. increased(늘어난)는 정반대라, '수확이 늘어나는데 식량이 부족하다'는 앞뒤가 안 맞는 말이 돼요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

④ prepared: 'to urge people to be prepared'는 '사람들에게 대비하라고 촉구하기 위해'예요. 재난을 경고하는 글이라 '대비된(prepared)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 가뭄 → 수확 감소(reduced) → 식량 부족·굶주림. increased(증가)면 앞뒤가 반대

questions.passage: The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts.  Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor.  The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be prepared.  Considering the continuation of climate change, experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② persist for decades(수십 년간 계속되다): 빈칸 앞에서 '단순하고 이따금 오는 가뭄이 아니라 심각한 가뭄'이라고 대비했으니, 오래 지속된다는 뜻이 와야 해요
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could ___'(전문가들은 우리가 마주한 상황이 단순히 이따금 오는 가뭄이 아니라 ___ 할 수 있는 심각한 가뭄이라고 경고한다). 'not just A but B(단순히 A가 아니라 B)' 구조로, '이따금 오는(occasional)' 가벼운 가뭄과 대비되는 '심각한(severe)' 가뭄이에요. 그러니 빈칸에는 '오래 계속된다'는 뜻이 들어가야 해요.

❌ ① disappear within days(며칠 안에 사라지다): 심각한 가뭄이라는 앞 내용과 반대예요.

✅ ② persist for decades(수십 년간 계속되다): '이따금 오는' 가뭄과 대비되는 '심각한' 가뭄의 특징으로 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ benefit local farmers(지역 농부들에게 이롭다): 가뭄이 이롭다는 것은 글의 흐름과 반대예요.

❌ ④ occur only rarely(아주 드물게만 일어나다): '이따금(occasional)'과 비슷한 뜻이라, 그것과 대비되는 빈칸에는 안 맞아요.
det.tip: 'not just 이따금 가뭄 but 심각한 가뭄' → 빈칸은 '오래 지속된다(수십 년)'는 뜻

questions.passage: As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize I am too late.  The shelves are already empty.  I manage my way to the side aisle, trying my luck.  Sometimes people place unwanted items in the wrong shelves.  Lucky!  I find a single case of water that someone abandoned there maybe yesterday, when it wasn’t such __________.  I reach for it, only to find it pulled away at the last second by a woman.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① a precious commodity(귀중한 물품): 지금은 물이 없어서 다들 다투는 상황인데, '어제까지만 해도 물이 아직 ___가 아니었을 때'라고 했으니 지금은 물이 '귀한 것'이 된 거예요
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'I find a single case of water that someone abandoned there maybe yesterday, when it wasn't such ___'(나는 누군가가 아마 어제 그곳에 버려둔 생수 한 상자를 발견한다. 그때는 물이 아직 ___가 아니었을 때다). 지금은 선반이 텅 비고 사람들이 물 한 병에 다투는 상황이에요. 즉 지금 물은 매우 귀해졌고, '어제까지는 아직 그렇게 귀하지 않았다'는 대비를 나타내야 해요.

✅ ① a precious commodity(귀중한 물품): 지금은 물이 귀해졌다는 상황과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② a common product(흔한 상품): '흔했을 때'라고 하면 말은 되지만, 빈칸은 지금 물이 '귀해졌다'는 대비를 강조하는 자리라 '귀중한 물품'이 더 정확해요.

❌ ③ a useless item(쓸모없는 물건): 물은 생존에 꼭 필요한 것이라 '쓸모없다'는 흐름과 반대예요.

❌ ④ a heavy container(무거운 용기): 물의 '가치'가 아니라 '무게'를 말하는 것이라 문맥과 안 맞아요.
det.tip: 지금은 물 쟁탈전 → 물이 귀해짐. '어제는 아직 ___가 아니었다' = 귀중한 물품(precious commodity)

✅ ④ 원문 'She is watching the TV, where a news anchor is talking about the flow crisis. This is what the media has been calling the drought'와 일치해요. 어머니는 가뭄(=flow crisis) 뉴스를 보고 있었어요. ←정답

questions.passage: Further Reading Hunger Stones In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought in 500 years in Europe, a stone known as a “hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along the Elbe River.  The stone had a sentence written on it that read: “If you see me, then cry. ” The hunger stones, found in rivers across central Europe, typically remain underwater.  However, when droughts occur and water levels retreat, these stones become visible.  The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts.  Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor.  The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be prepared.  Considering the continuation of climate change, experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could persist for decades.

det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 'The hunger stones ... typically remain underwater. However, when droughts occur and water levels retreat, these stones become visible'로, 헝거 스톤은 평소 물속에 잠겨 있다가 가뭄 때 드러나요. 진술은 정반대예요.

✅ ② 원문 'In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought in 500 years in Europe'와 일치해요. 2022년 유럽 가뭄이 500년 만에 가장 심각했어요. ←정답

❌ ③ 원문은 'by 2050, 75 percent of the global population could suffer from the effects of drought'로, '절반'이 아니라 '75퍼센트'예요. 숫자가 달라요.

❌ ④ 원문 'If you see me, then cry'와 'The words ... are believed to warn of these hardships'로, 문구는 고난을 경고하는 내용이지 축하 메시지가 아니에요.

유엔은 2050년까지 전 세계 인구의 절반이 가뭄 피해를 겪을 것으로 예측했다.

questions.passage: The kitchen tap makes strange sounds.  It coughs.  It spits once, and then goes silent.  “Mom,” I shout out into the living room, “water is not coming out. ” “Alyssa, shush! ” Mom says.  She is watching the TV, where a news anchor is talking about the “flow crisis. ” This is what the media has been calling the drought ever since people got tired of hearing the word “drought. ” Now the crisis is entering a new stage.  We have no running water out of the tap.  “To the mall! ” says Uncle Basil.  My little brother Garrett and I jump in our uncle’s truck.  As we pull into the parking lot, we can see the crowd.  “You two go in.  I’ll meet you inside,” Uncle Basil says.  Inside it’s like Black Friday at its worst — but today it’s not televisions and video games people are after.  What I see in the carts in the checkout line are mostly water bottles.  The essentials of life.  There is a look of impatience on the faces of the people in line.  There is even hostility, hidden by a thin layer of politeness.  Even that politeness is stretched thin.  As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize I am too late.  The shelves are already empty.  I manage my way to the side aisle, trying my luck.  Sometimes people place unwanted items in the wrong shelves.  Lucky!  I find a single case of water that someone abandoned there maybe yesterday, when it wasn’t such a precious commodity.  I reach for it, only to find it pulled away at the last second by a woman.  She stacks it on top of her cart like a crown on top of her canned goods.  “I’m sorry, but we were here first,” she says.  And then her daughter steps forward — a girl I recognize from soccer — Hali Hartling.  As her mother pulls their cart away, Hali leans closer to me.  “I’m sorry about that, Alyssa. ” “Didn’t I share my water with you at the practice last week? ” I point out to her.  “Maybe you could return the favor and share a few bottles with me. ” She looks back to her mother, who’s already moving down the aisle, then turns back to me shaking her head.  And then she gets a little bit red in the face, and turns to leave before it becomes a deep flush.  I look for Garrett, whom I find in the frozen aisle.  Then I see something.  Just past the frozen vegetables and ice cream, there is a case packed with ice.  I open the door and reach for a bag.  “What are you doing?  We need water, not ice,” he reminds me.  “Ice is water.  Just help me,” I tell him.  Garrett and I put one bag of ice after another into our cart, until it is piled as high as it can get.  By now other people have taken notice and begin to empty the ice case.  The cart is ridiculously heavy now, and almost impossible to push.  Then, a man in a business suit comes up behind us.  He smiles.  “Looks like you could use some help. ” He doesn’t wait for us to answer before grabbing the cart’s handle.  “Thank you for helping us,” I tell him.  “Not a problem.  We all need to help one another. ” He smiles again, and I return the smile.  It is good to know that difficult times can bring out the best in people.  I decide that one favor deserves another.  “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourself,” I suggest.  His smile does not fade.  “I have a better idea,” he says.  “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourselves, and I’ll keep the rest. ” Alyssa. ” For a moment I think he is joking, but then realize he is serious.  “Excuse me? ” He is still smiling, but his eyes scare me.  As long as his hands are firmly locked on the handle of our cart, there is nothing to prove that it’s ours and not his.  “Is there a problem here? ” It is Uncle Basil.  He has arrived just in time.  “Not at all. ” The man looks at the ice with a bitter face, then leaves.  *The above is a shortened version of the opening of the novel Dry (2018).  It tells the story of a girl who has to make tough choices for her family during a disastrous California drought.  Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal.  Provided that the factors contributing to water shortages worldwide are not addressed, including climate change, population growth, and using too much water for agriculture, it is possible that this story can become a reality.  Further Reading Hunger Stones In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought in 500 years in Europe, a stone known as a “hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along the Elbe River.  The stone had a sentence written on it that read: “If you see me, then cry. ” The hunger stones, found in rivers across central Europe, typically remain underwater.  However, when droughts occur and water levels retreat, these stones become visible.  The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts.  Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor.  The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be prepared.  Considering the continuation of climate change, experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could persist for decades.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ suffer from the effects of drought(가뭄의 영향으로 고통받다): 기후 변화에 대한 큰 조치가 없으면 인구의 75%가 겪을 부정적 결과여야 해요
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'The United Nations has predicted that by 2050, 75 percent of the global population could ___ unless significant action is taken to address climate change.'(유엔은 기후 변화에 대응하는 중대한 조치가 취해지지 않는 한, 2050년까지 전 세계 인구의 75퍼센트가 ___ 할 수 있다고 예측했다). 'unless(~하지 않는 한)'는 조건이 안 지켜지면 나쁜 일이 생긴다는 뜻이라, 빈칸에는 부정적인 결과가 와야 해요. 앞에서 가뭄이 수확 감소·식량 부족·굶주림을 일으킨다고 했어요.

❌ ① enjoy abundant clean water supplies(풍부하고 깨끗한 물을 누리다): 좋은 일이라, 경고하는 흐름과 반대예요.

❌ ② forget the dangers of climate change(기후 변화의 위험을 잊다): 인구가 겪을 '피해'가 아니라 태도라, 예측 내용과 안 맞아요.

❌ ③ benefit from advanced farming methods(발전된 농법의 혜택을 받다): 긍정적 결과라 흐름과 반대예요.

✅ ④ suffer from the effects of drought(가뭄의 영향으로 고통받다): 조치가 없으면 생길 부정적 결과로 딱 맞아요. ←정답
det.tip: 'unless(~하지 않으면)' + 경고 글 → 빈칸은 부정적 결과(가뭄 피해로 고통)

ch: forget the dangers of climate change
suffer from the effects of drought

questions.passage: ” He doesn’t wait for us to answer before grabbing the cart’s handle.  “Thank you for helping us,” I tell him.  “Not a problem.  __________. ” He smiles again, and I return the smile.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"우리는 모두 서로를 도와야 한다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) all, another, help, need, one, to, We 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: We all need to help one another
det.analysis:
주어는 'We(우리는)'예요. 그 뒤에 '모두'라는 뜻의 all을 붙여 'We all(우리는 모두)'로 강조해요.

'~해야 한다'는 need to로 나타내요: need(필요로 하다) + to help(돕는 것을) → '도와야 한다'.

'서로를'은 one another라는 표현으로 나타내요. one과 another를 이 순서로 붙여 '서로'라는 뜻이 돼요.

순서대로 이으면 We / all / need / to / help / one / another → 'We all need to help one another'.
det.tip: '~해야 한다' = need to + 동사원형 / '서로' = one another

questions.wa: We all need to help one another
accept: We all need to help one another

questions.passage: *The above is a shortened version of the opening of the novel Dry (2018).  It tells the story of a girl who has to make tough choices for her family during a disastrous California drought.  Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal.  Provided that the factors contributing to water shortages worldwide are not addressed, including climate change, population growth, and using too much water for agriculture, it is possible that this story can become a reality.  Further Reading Hunger Stones In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought in 500 years in Europe, a stone ①<u>knowing</u> as a “hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along the Elbe River.  The stone had a sentence written on it that read: “If you see me, then cry.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: knowing → known: 'a stone (that is) known as ~(~라고 알려진 돌)'처럼 돌이 '알려지는' 쪽(수동)이라 과거분사 known
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'a stone ①<u>knowing</u> as a hunger stone was found in a Czech town along the Elbe River.'예요. '엘베 강가의 한 체코 마을에서 헝거 스톤이라고 알려진 돌 하나가 발견되었다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 밑줄 친 말은 앞의 명사 'a stone(돌)'을 꾸며 줘요. 돌은 사람들에게 '알려지는' 쪽이에요. 이렇게 '~되는(당하는)'이라는 수동의 뜻으로 명사를 꾸밀 때는 과거분사(-ed형)를 써요. 'be known as ~(~로 알려지다)'라는 표현을 떠올리면, 'a stone (that is) known as a hunger stone(헝거 스톤이라고 알려진 돌)'처럼 known이 맞아요.

현재분사 knowing(-ing형)은 '알고 있는'이라는 능동의 뜻이라 여기엔 안 맞아요. 돌이 무언가를 '아는' 게 아니니까요.

따라서 knowing을 known으로 고쳐야 해요.
det.tip: '~라고 알려진' = (be) known as ~ → 수동의 뜻이라 과거분사 known

"그녀의 원치 않은 모험은 물 공급이 재개되고 삶이 정상으로 돌아올 때 끝난다." (15단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) adventure, and, back, ends, Her, is, life, normal, resumes, supply, the, to, unwanted, water, when 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 15단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal
det.analysis:
문장의 주어는 'Her unwanted adventure(그녀의 원치 않은 모험)'예요. Her → unwanted → adventure 순서로 놓아요.

동사는 '끝난다'라는 뜻의 ends예요. 주어가 단수라 -s를 붙여 ends로 써요.

'~할 때'는 접속사 when으로 이어요. when 뒤에는 두 가지 일이 and로 연결돼요.

첫째, '물 공급이 재개되다'는 the water supply(물 공급) + resumes(재개되다)로 써요.

둘째, '삶이 정상으로 돌아오다'는 life is back to normal이라는 표현으로 써요: life(삶) + is back to(~로 돌아오다) + normal(정상).

두 일을 and로 이으면 'when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal'이 돼요.

순서대로 이으면 Her / unwanted / adventure / ends / when / the / water / supply / resumes / and / life / is / back / to / normal.
det.tip: '~할 때' = when + 문장 / 두 가지 상황을 and로 연결(A resumes and B is back to normal)

questions.wa: Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal
accept: Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal
Her unwanted adventure ends when life is back to normal and the water supply resumes

[ are / bottles / carts / checkout / I / in / in / line / mostly / see / the / the / water / What ] (14단어) (영어로)

det.korean: What I see in the carts in the checkout line are mostly water bottles
det.analysis:
'내가 보는 것은'은 What I see로 시작해요. What은 '~하는 것'이라는 뜻으로, 이 덩어리 전체가 문장의 주어가 돼요: What(~하는 것) + I(내가) + see(보는).

'계산대 줄에 있는 카트 안에서'는 장소를 나타내는 두 개의 전치사구예요: in the carts(카트 안에서) + in the checkout line(계산대 줄에 있는). 이 순서로 붙여요.

주어(What I see ...)가 끝나면 동사 are를 놓아요. '~것들'이 대부분 생수병이라는 뜻이라 are로 이어요.

'대부분 생수병이다'는 mostly(대부분) + water(물) + bottles(병)로 써요.

순서대로 이으면 What / I / see / in / the / carts / in / the / checkout / line / are / mostly / water / bottles.
det.tip: '내가 보는 것은' = What I see(주어 덩어리) → 뒤에 동사 are로 이음

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"나는 하나의 호의가 또 다른 호의를 받을 만하다고 생각한다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) another, decide, deserves, favor, I, one, that 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: I decide that one favor deserves another
det.analysis:
주어는 'I(나는)', 동사는 '생각한다/결정한다'라는 뜻의 decide예요.

'~라고'는 생각의 내용을 이어 주는 접속사 that으로 나타내요: I decide that ~(나는 ~라고 생각한다).

that이 이끄는 내용의 주어는 'one favor(하나의 호의)'예요. one(하나의) + favor(호의) 순서로 놓아요.

'~을 받을 만하다'는 동사 deserves로 나타내요. 주어 one favor가 단수라 -s를 붙여 deserves로 써요.

'또 다른 호의를'은 another(또 다른 것)로 나타내요. 여기서 another는 'another favor(또 다른 호의)'를 대신하는 말이에요.

순서대로 이으면 I / decide / that / one / favor / deserves / another → 'I decide that one favor deserves another'.
det.tip: '~라고 생각하다' = decide that + 문장 / 주어 one favor(단수) → 동사 deserves

questions.wa: I decide that one favor deserves another
accept: I decide that one favor deserves another
